data.one_liner: Inspects active network interfaces, internet capability, validation, metering, and bandwidth.
data.what_it_does: A Flutter plugin providing low-level, system-driven visibility into active network interfaces on a device. It allows apps to inspect multiple simultaneous networks, check internet capability, validation state, metering, and bandwidth estimates.
use_when: You need to know whether a connection actually has internet access (e.g., captive portal detection).
You need to distinguish metered from unmetered connections to adapt data usage.
You need bandwidth estimates to adjust media quality on Android.
You need to reason about multiple simultaneous network interfaces.
avoid_when: You need broad platform coverage across Windows, Linux, or Web.
You only need a basic connection type check and do not require interface-level details.
strengths: Provides detailed inspection of multiple simultaneous network interfaces.
Exposes internet capability, validation, and metering status across platforms.
Offers real-time network change streams using native event-driven implementations.
weaknesses: Limited platform support compared to some alternatives (Android, iOS, macOS only).
Bandwidth estimates (`downLinkKbps`, `upLinkKbps`) are only available on Android.
VPN detection behaves differently or is not exposed as a distinct interface type on iOS and macOS.
data.setup_notes: Requires Flutter 3.44+ and Dart 3.12+. No special extra manual platform permissions are documented beyond standard plugin inclusion.

alternatives.name: connectivity_plus
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick it if you need broader platform coverage including Windows, Linux, and Web, or only require general connection types.
